bio.topic: Photosynthesis: equations and uses of glucose

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.hint: Think about the gas animals breathe out.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the green pigment that absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.
questions.hint: It is found inside chloroplasts and gives leaves their colour.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the organelle in plant cells where photosynthesis takes place.
questions.hint: Look for the green structures inside palisade cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the correct word equation for photosynthesis?
questions.hint: The reactants are taken in by leaves and roots; one product is a sugar.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the balanced symbol equation for photosynthesis?
questions.hint: Count the carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms on both sides.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In the balanced symbol equation for photosynthesis, how many molecules of carbon dioxide are needed to make one molecule of glucose?
questions.hint: How many carbon atoms are in one glucose molecule?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: If a plant uses 12 molecules of carbon dioxide in photosynthesis, how many molecules of oxygen are released?
questions.hint: Compare the numbers in front of CO₂ and O₂ in the balanced equation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Describe the energy transfer that chlorophyll makes possible in photosynthesis.
options: light energy → chemical energy in glucose
questions.answer: light energy → chemical energy in glucose
questions.hint: Where is the energy stored once the sugar has been made?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which colours of light are absorbed most by chlorophyll?
questions.hint: Leaves look green because that colour is mostly reflected.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Plants convert glucose into which insoluble substance for storage in leaves, seeds and roots?
questions.hint: Potatoes and rice contain large amounts of it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which sugar, made from glucose, is transported around the plant in the phloem?
questions.hint: It is the same sugar we buy as table sugar.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Plants use glucose to make which substance that strengthens their cell walls?
questions.hint: It is a structural carbohydrate made of long chains of glucose.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Together with glucose, which mineral ions do plants absorb from the soil to make amino acids for proteins?
questions.hint: Proteins contain an element that carbohydrates do not have.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A leaf is tested for starch with iodine solution. What colour shows that starch is present?
questions.hint: Iodine solution itself starts orange-brown.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why plants store glucose as starch rather than as glucose.
questions.hint: Think about solubility and the effect on water movement into cells by osmosis.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Describe three ways a plant uses the glucose made in photosynthesis, apart from storing it as starch.
questions.hint: Consider energy release, building materials and substances in seeds.

bss.topic: Ditadura: milagre econômico, resistência e cultura

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O período chamado de “milagre econômico” brasileiro ocorreu aproximadamente entre quais anos?
questions.hint: Foi durante os governos mais repressivos da ditadura, antes da crise do petróleo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Durante o milagre econômico, o PIB do Brasil cresceu, em média, cerca de quanto por ano?
questions.hint: Foram taxas de crescimento muito altas, entre as maiores do mundo na época.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi uma das principais fontes de dinheiro para financiar o crescimento do milagre?
options: Doações de outros países sem juros
Venda de terras para a população
questions.hint: Pense no problema da dívida que apareceu depois.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase ficou associada à política de renda da época?
options: “Fazer o bolo crescer para depois dividir”
questions.answer: “Fazer o bolo crescer para depois dividir”
questions.hint: A ideia era primeiro crescer e só depois distribuir a riqueza.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi uma consequência negativa do milagre econômico?
options: Aumento da concentração de renda e da dívida externa
questions.answer: Aumento da concentração de renda e da dívida externa
questions.hint: Pense em quem ficou com a maior parte do “bolo”.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual acontecimento internacional de 1973 ajudou a encerrar o milagre econômico?
options: A queda do Muro de Berlim
O fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial
questions.hint: O Brasil importava grande parte de um combustível essencial.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual rodovia, aberta na região amazônica, foi um dos símbolos das grandes obras do período?
questions.hint: O nome indica que ela atravessaria a Amazônia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual ato institucional, de dezembro de 1968, endureceu a repressão e ampliou a censura?
questions.hint: Foi o mais duro dos atos institucionais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamou o movimento cultural de 1967–1968 que misturou ritmos brasileiros, guitarra elétrica e influências pop?
questions.hint: O nome lembra o clima de um país tropical.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual sigla designa a “música popular brasileira”, gênero de muitas canções de protesto?
questions.hint: São as iniciais das três palavras.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que muitos compositores usavam metáforas e duplo sentido nas letras durante a ditadura?
options: Para vender mais discos no exterior
questions.hint: As letras eram analisadas antes de serem liberadas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual movimento de guerrilha rural ocorreu na região do rio Araguaia no início dos anos 1970?
questions.hint: Os outros movimentos aconteceram no século XIX.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas foi uma forma de resistência NÃO armada à ditadura?
options: Passeatas estudantis e canções de protesto
questions.answer: Passeatas estudantis e canções de protesto
questions.hint: Procure a forma de oposição que usava a voz e a arte.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Avalie o “milagre econômico”: apresente um ponto positivo e um ponto negativo e conclua se ele beneficiou toda a população.
questions.hint: Pense em crescimento, obras e empregos, mas também em salários, desigualdade e dívida.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a música se tornou uma forma importante de resistência durante a ditadura.
questions.hint: Considere o alcance dos festivais e do rádio e as estratégias contra a censura.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Compare a luta armada e a resistência cultural como formas de oposição ao regime militar.
questions.hint: Pense nos objetivos, nos riscos e no apoio da população a cada uma.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to Taylor, what is the main thing that motivates workers?
questions.hint: Taylor saw workers as 'economic people'.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the name given to Taylor's approach to management?
questions.hint: He used careful measurement and study to find the best way to work.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is piece rate?
options: Paying workers a fixed amount for each unit produced
Paying a share of the company's profits
questions.answer: Paying workers a fixed amount for each unit produced
questions.hint: Pay depends on output, not time.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A worker is paid $0.50 per unit on piece rate and produces 240 units in a day. Calculate the worker's pay for the day, in dollars.
questions.hint: Multiply the rate by the number of units.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A factory changes from paying $80 per day to a piece rate of $0.40 per unit. How many units must a worker produce to earn the same as before?
questions.hint: Divide the daily pay by the rate per unit.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Taylor used time-and-motion studies mainly to…
options: find the most efficient way to do each task
questions.answer: find the most efficient way to do each task
questions.hint: He timed workers and broke jobs into small steps.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a limitation of Taylor's approach?
options: Repetitive, simple tasks can be boring and demotivating
Workers are given too much responsibility
Workers learn too many different skills
questions.answer: Repetitive, simple tasks can be boring and demotivating
questions.hint: Think about doing the same small task all day.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Herzberg's two-factor theory, what are factors such as pay and working conditions called?
questions.hint: They prevent dissatisfaction rather than motivate.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to Herzberg, what happens if hygiene factors are poor?
questions.hint: Hygiene factors only remove a negative feeling.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is a motivator in Herzberg's theory?
questions.hint: Motivators relate to the job itself and personal growth.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is a hygiene factor in Herzberg's theory?
questions.hint: Hygiene factors are about the job's environment, not the work itself.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Giving a worker more challenging tasks and more responsibility is called…
questions.hint: It adds depth to a job, not just more tasks of the same level.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Herzberg argued that improving hygiene factors alone will…
options: remove dissatisfaction but not motivate workers
questions.answer: remove dissatisfaction but not motivate workers
questions.hint: Remember the two separate sets of factors.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is a key difference between Taylor's and Herzberg's views on pay?
options: Taylor saw pay as the main motivator; Herzberg saw it as a hygiene factor
Both saw pay as the most important motivator
Herzberg recommended piece rate for all jobs
Taylor believed pay did not matter
questions.answer: Taylor saw pay as the main motivator; Herzberg saw it as a hygiene factor
questions.hint: Compare where each theorist puts money.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A clothing factory pays its machinists piece rate. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of this method for the business.
questions.hint: Think about output and also about quality and safety.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A software company pays high salaries but has high staff turnover. Using Herzberg's theory, recommend how the company could improve motivation. Justify your answer.
questions.hint: Salary is already good, so which type of factor is missing?

chem.topic: Empirical and molecular formulae; percentage purity and composition

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is meant by the empirical formula of a compound?
options: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in the compound
The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule
The mass of one mole of the compound
The percentage by mass of each element
questions.answer: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in the compound
questions.hint: 'Simplest' is the key word.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the empirical formula of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.
questions.hint: Divide all the subscripts by their highest common factor.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the empirical formula of ethene, C₂H₄.
questions.hint: Divide both numbers by the same factor.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of magnesium in magnesium oxide, MgO. (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.hint: Divide the mass of magnesium by the Mr and multiply by 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃. (Ar: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.hint: Count how many nitrogen atoms there are in the formula first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of water in hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O. (Ar: Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.hint: Find the Mr of the whole formula and of the five water molecules.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A sample of a hydrocarbon contains 2.4 g of carbon and 0.6 g of hydrogen. Deduce its empirical formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
questions.hint: Convert each mass to moles, then divide by the smallest.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A hydrocarbon has the empirical formula CH₃ and a relative molecular mass of 30. Deduce its molecular formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
questions.hint: How many CH₃ units fit into 30?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 1.2 g of magnesium is burned and forms 2.0 g of magnesium oxide. Deduce the empirical formula of the oxide. (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.hint: Work out the mass of oxygen that combined first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 5.6 g of iron combines with 2.4 g of oxygen. Deduce the empirical formula of the iron oxide. (Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16)
questions.hint: If the mole ratio is not whole, multiply both numbers by 2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Calculate its empirical formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.hint: Assume 100 g of compound, so the percentages become masses.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound has the empirical formula CH₂O and a relative molecular mass of 180. Deduce its molecular formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.hint: Find the mass of one CH₂O unit and divide 180 by it.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound contains 52.2% carbon, 13.0% hydrogen and 34.8% oxygen by mass. Calculate its empirical formula. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.hint: Divide each percentage by Ar, then divide by the smallest answer.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An 8.0 g sample of impure aspirin contains 6.0 g of pure aspirin. Calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
questions.hint: Percentage purity = mass of pure substance ÷ mass of sample × 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 25.0 g of impure calcium carbonate is heated and produces 8.8 g of carbon dioxide: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the percentage purity of the calcium carbonate. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CO₂ = 44)
questions.hint: Find the moles of CO₂, then the mass of CaCO₃ that must have reacted.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why two different compounds can have the same empirical formula but different molecular formulae. Use an example in your answer.
questions.hint: Compare a small and a large molecule whose atoms are in the same ratio.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which flowchart symbol is used to show the start or end of an algorithm?
questions.hint: Think of the shape that looks like a pill or oval.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which flowchart symbol represents a decision?
questions.hint: A decision has two exits: Yes and No.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which flowchart symbol represents input or output, such as INPUT name or OUTPUT total?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which flowchart symbol represents a process, such as total ← total + 1?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the term for writing an algorithm in structured English-like statements that are not tied to a specific programming language.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of the three basic programming constructs means instructions are carried out one after another in order?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A diamond in a flowchart with one exit looping back to an earlier step most likely shows which construct?
questions.hint: Going back to repeat steps is called…

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Consider the pseudocode:
x ← 4
y ← x * 3
x ← y - 5
OUTPUT x
What is output?
questions.hint: Work line by line and keep track of each variable.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Consider the pseudocode:
total ← 0
FOR i ← 1 TO 4
  total ← total + i
NEXT i
OUTPUT total
What is output?
questions.hint: Add each value of i from 1 to 4.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Consider the pseudocode:
count ← 0
n ← 20
WHILE n > 1
  n ← n DIV 2
  count ← count + 1
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT count
What is output? (DIV is integer division.)
questions.hint: Trace n: 20, 10, … and count how many times the loop body runs.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Consider the pseudocode:
INPUT mark
IF mark >= 50 THEN
  OUTPUT "Pass"
ELSE
  OUTPUT "Fail"
ENDIF
What is output if mark is 50?
questions.hint: Check carefully what >= means.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which construct is used in the pseudocode IF temperature > 30 THEN OUTPUT "Hot" ENDIF?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which pseudocode loop is most suitable when the number of repetitions is known in advance?
questions.hint: Which loop uses a counter from a start value to an end value?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a key difference between a WHILE loop and a REPEAT … UNTIL loop?
options: REPEAT … UNTIL always runs its body at least once
WHILE always runs at least once
questions.answer: REPEAT … UNTIL always runs its body at least once
questions.hint: Where is the condition checked in each loop?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Write pseudocode for an algorithm that asks the user to input 5 numbers and outputs the largest number.
questions.hint: Store the first number as the largest, then compare each new number with it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe two advantages of representing an algorithm as a flowchart rather than pseudocode.

econ.topic: Market failure: externalities, private and social costs and benefits

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is an externality?
options: A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the transaction
A tax paid by firms to the government
The price a consumer pays for a good
A cost paid only by the producer
questions.answer: A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the transaction

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A factory pays for its raw materials, wages and electricity. These are examples of…
questions.hint: Who pays these costs?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which formula correctly defines social cost?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which formula correctly defines social benefit?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Noise from a nightclub that keeps nearby residents awake is an example of…
questions.hint: The residents are not part of the nightclub's transactions.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: When a person is vaccinated, others are less likely to catch the disease. This is an example of…

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for goods, such as education, that create positive externalities and tend to be under-consumed in a free market.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for goods, such as cigarettes, that create negative externalities and tend to be over-consumed in a free market.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm's private cost of producing a batch of goods is $500. The pollution it creates causes $200 of damage to local residents. Calculate the social cost.
questions.hint: Social cost = private cost + external cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A student's private benefit from a university course is valued at $40,000. The external benefit to society is $15,000. Calculate the social benefit, in dollars.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The social cost of driving a car one kilometre is $0.90. The private cost to the driver is $0.60. Calculate the external cost per kilometre, in dollars.
questions.hint: External cost = social cost − private cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a free market with negative externalities in production, the good is likely to be…
options: Over-produced compared to the socially optimal level
Under-produced compared to the socially optimal level
Produced at exactly the social optimum
questions.answer: Over-produced compared to the socially optimal level
questions.hint: Producers ignore costs they do not pay themselves.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Externalities are a type of market failure because…
options: Resources are not allocated in the best way for society
questions.answer: Resources are not allocated in the best way for society

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which government policy would most directly reduce a negative production externality such as pollution?
options: A tax on the polluting output
A subsidy to the polluting firm
questions.answer: A tax on the polluting output

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain why the free market tends to under-provide education. Refer to private and external benefits in your answer.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain two consequences for third parties of a new airport being built near a town.
questions.hint: Think about both costs and benefits for people living nearby.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The students' books were left on the bus.
The student's books' were left on the bus.
The students books' were left on the bus.
The students's books were left on the bus.
questions.answer: The students' books were left on the bus.
questions.hint: For a plural noun ending in -s, where does the apostrophe go?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: "___ going to be late if we don't hurry."

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: "The storm had a huge ___ on the village."
questions.hint: One is usually a noun, the other usually a verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence contains a comma splice?
options: It was raining, we stayed inside.
It was raining, so we stayed inside.
Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
It was raining; we stayed inside.
questions.answer: It was raining, we stayed inside.
questions.hint: Look for two main clauses joined only by a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is spelt correctly?
questions.hint: One collar, two sleeves.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling of this word: "definately".

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling of this word: "recieve".

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence shows correct subject–verb agreement?
options: Neither of the answers is correct.
Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answer are correct.
Neither of the answers be correct.
questions.answer: Neither of the answers is correct.
questions.hint: What is the actual subject of the sentence?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct option: "She ___ the report before the meeting started."

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The museum was closed; we visited the park instead.
The museum was; closed we visited the park.
The museum was closed; and we visited the park.
questions.answer: The museum was closed; we visited the park instead.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: "I would ___ gone if I had known."
questions.hint: Say it slowly: it sounds like one word but is spelt as another.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The dog wagged it is tail.
questions.hint: Does the sentence mean "it is"?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: suprised → surprised; beleived → believed; definately → definitely; peacefull → peaceful; untill → until
questions.hint: Read slowly, one word at a time, as if proofreading an exam answer.
questions.text: When I first arrived at the coastal town, I was suprised by how quiet it was. The harbour was almost empty, and the only sound was the wind against the boats. I had beleived it would be busy, but the season had finished. It was definately the most peacefull place I had ever visited, and I wanted to stay untill spring.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain a systematic method for proofreading a piece of extended writing in an exam.
questions.hint: Think about reading for different types of error at different times.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Identify and correct the errors in this sentence, then explain each correction: "Their was alot of people at the concert, and everyone enjoyed themself."

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which spelling of this word is correct?

en_lit.topic: Short stories: comparing themes across Stories of Ourselves Vol. 3

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: When comparing themes across two short stories, what should a strong paragraph do?
options: Discuss both stories and link them with comparative connectives
Retell the plot of each story in turn
Focus only on the story you prefer
questions.answer: Discuss both stories and link them with comparative connectives

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which connective best introduces a similarity between two stories?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which connective best introduces a difference between two stories?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: State the literary term for the central idea or message that a writer explores in a text.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which of the following is a theme rather than a plot event?
questions.hint: A theme is an idea, not something that happens.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What makes a quotation "apt" evidence in a comparison essay?
options: It is short and directly supports the point being made
It is the longest quotation available
It comes from the first page
It includes the name of the author
questions.answer: It is short and directly supports the point being made

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which is the most effective way to embed a quotation?
options: The narrator feels "trapped" by the city around her.
questions.answer: The narrator feels "trapped" by the city around her.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Two stories both explore the theme of childhood, but one is nostalgic and the other is fearful. What is being compared here?
options: The writers' attitudes to the same theme
questions.answer: The writers' attitudes to the same theme

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which of these sentences shows the best comparative analysis?
options: While both writers present loss, the first uses silence to show grief, whereas the second uses violent imagery.
The first story is sad. The second story is also sad.
I liked the second story more than the first.
questions.answer: While both writers present loss, the first uses silence to show grief, whereas the second uses violent imagery.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In an exam answer comparing short stories, what does "AO2"-style analysis usually focus on?
options: How language, structure and form create meaning
The historical facts of the author's life
questions.answer: How language, structure and form create meaning

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: State the term for a story's ending that leaves the outcome uncertain for the reader.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why might two writers set stories in very different places but explore the same theme?
options: To show the theme is universal across different lives
Because they were not allowed to use the same setting
questions.answer: To show the theme is universal across different lives

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which is the best way to structure a comparison essay on two stories?
options: Point-by-point, comparing both stories within each paragraph
All of story A, then all of story B, with no links
Only the introduction compares the stories
questions.answer: Point-by-point, comparing both stories within each paragraph

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A writer ends a story with a symbol, such as a closed door. What is the best way to write about this in a comparison?
options: Explain what the symbol suggests about the theme and contrast it with the other story's ending
Describe what the door looks like
Ignore it, as endings are not important
questions.answer: Explain what the symbol suggests about the theme and contrast it with the other story's ending

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Choose two short stories you have studied. Compare how each writer presents a theme they share, using a short embedded quotation from each.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain why selecting a small number of short, precise quotations is often more effective than using long quotations in a comparison essay.
